items.title: Yatai 8
items.description: An endless loop in a dark Japanese corridor. Observe every detail carefully: if everything looks normal, keep walking. If you notice even the slightest anomaly, turn back immediately. Escape the loop before it's too late.

items.title: Tales From Eternity - Interactive Preview
items.description: Step into the universe of Tales From Eternity and experience the complete first two chapters through an atmospheric digital reader.

items.title: Starjaunt
items.description: You start with a shuttle.Not a warship. Not a legend. A shuttle, a modest hold, and enough fuel to reach somewhere that isn't here.What happens after that is genuinely up to you. Starjaunt is an open galaxy of forty-four star systems, nine factions with their own grudges and their own ships, and a war that keeps moving whether or not you're involved in it. You can spend the whole game hauling grain and never fire a shot. You can spend it taking systems by force. Most people do something in between and find out what that makes them.[hr][/hr]Pick a life, or don'tMerchant. Buy low, sell high, watch prices move as the war strangles supply lines. Trade up from a shuttle to a freighter to a hold that pays for itself.Miner. Work the asteroid belts, sell ore to refineries, stay out of everyone's politics.Bounty hunter. Hunt people who don't want to be found, across a six-part arc that gets more complicated the closer you get.Spy. Thirteen missions of intelligence work — planted evidence, two-stage extractions, freighter interdictions, and bribes that show up in your ledger as negative pay. Nobody stays clean.Combat pilot. Fly for a flag. Take contracts, take systems, take losses.Fleet commander. You don't need a carrier to stop flying alone. Make friends who fly your wing for nothing, hire guns at the bar who fly it for a fee, or earn enough trust from a faction's command that they stop handing you contracts and start handing you berths.Nine factions, and none of them are simply rightThe Federation — order and duty, expressed as slow ships with too much armor and a tariff schedule for everything.The Rebel Alliance — speed as armor, freedom as a grievance, captured tech held together with conviction.The Free Frontier — farmers, ice-miners and free-port harbormasters who want to be left alone and are squeezed by everyone. They fight defensively and they remember who helped.The Helios Combine — a megacorp that owns the mines, the patents and the foundries, sells arms to both sides, and does not want the war to end. Drone swarms, because people are expensive.The Artifact Order — monastic zealots who hold the Precursor ruins sacred and will ram your hull to prove it.The Federation Bastion — the hardliner splinter that thinks the Federation went soft. Siege doctrine, scorched earth, no negotiated peace, ever.Pirates, the Merchant Guild, and the Independent worlds that keep their heads down while everyone else fights.Each faction's mission arc unlocks its own hulls, one ship at a time, behind its own missions — fifty-four ships and forty-three weapon and outfit systems across the roster. Fly Federation long enough and you'll be trusted with a carrier. Fly for the Order and you'll be trusted with something stranger.The war moves without youSystems aren't decorations with a flag painted on. Control is a live number, and player missions push it. Take enough of a frontier system for the Rebels and it turns green on the star map — and then the markets restock from Rebel suppliers, Rebel patrols replace Federation ones, prices shift, standings follow, and the contracts on offer change with them. Contested systems spawn both sides at once and let them fight it out in front of you.Nothing about that is scripted. It falls out of one number per system, and it means the galaxy you're flying through in hour forty is not the one you started in.Nobody out here flies on railsThe pilots you fight weren't handed a patrol route and a state machine. They were trained — a neural network taught to fly by reinforcement learning, in simulation systems built for the purpose, until pirates learned to hunt traders and patrols learned to protect them.What comes out the other side is pilots with personalities. Some are reckless and some won't commit. Some break off a fight they're losing and some absolutely will not. They misjudge, they overextend, and now and then they do something you wouldn't have thought of. You end up reading them the way you'd read a person, because in the only sense that matters at knife-fight range, that's what the training produced.Land, and step outDocking isn't a menu. Set down and you walk the world on foot — desert outposts under prefab domes, forested colonies with lakes and lumber, company towns, garrisons, free ports. Find the fuel depot. Argue with the mechanic. Sell your haul at the warehouse and learn at the bar what's worth carrying next.You don't have to fly aloneThere are three ways to stop, and they cost you different things.Make friends. Twelve companions can be earned across the storylines — a cashiered Federation ace who flies angry, a homesteader who doesn't forget a kindness, a smuggler paying off a debt in escort hours. They fly their own ships, talk to you in combat, walk beside you when you land, and each has their own mission arc.Hire guns. Every bar has a wingman desk. Pay the fee and a veteran, a rookie or a mercenary flies your wing until they die or you let them go. When a hire dies you're out the money. When a friend dies you're out a friend — and there's a ledger for the ones who don't come back.Earn a fleet. Fly long enough for a faction and its command stops offering you contracts and starts offering you berths. Federation carrier certification, signed off by an officer who's watched you work. A converted capital hull the Alliance names you the first captain of. A deck on a Free Fleet carrier, handed over by a pirate king who decides you've earned it. Nobody sells you a fleet. You're given one, by people who had to be convinced.And past the last charted jumpSomething built the ruins at Tau Ceti and seeded the exotic matter at the fringe. It is gone, but not entirely.Out beyond Sanctum, through a jump that isn't stable, the Rift holds something dormant that answers when the relics are disturbed. It doesn't trade. It doesn't bargain. It doesn't hate you. It responds — and when it starts responding, the Federation's quarrel with the Rebels stops looking like the important story.How that ends is the one choice the game really asks you for. Seal it. Wake it. Or take it apart and use it.[hr][/hr]At a glance44 star systems across seven distinct regions — core worlds, contested borderlands, frontier reaches, company space, fortress systems, a monastic road, and a deep nobody comes back from134 missions, including six full faction campaigns that converge on the same battles from opposite sides54 ships and 43 weapons and outfits, most gated behind the factions that build themA live faction war that redraws the map, the markets and the trafficEnemy and civilian pilots flown by a reinforcement-learning policy rather than a scriptOn-foot exploration of every world you land on — deserts, ice fields, gardens, company towns, free ports12 companions to earn, mercenaries to hire, and fleets handed to you by factions that learned to trust you — companions who die stay deadThree endingsWindows, macOS and LinuxKeyboard only at launch.

items.title: Wickling
items.description: A cheerful 8-bit kingdom platformer with a candle for a head and something wrong underneath. World maps, power-up suits, fortresses and airships in the spirit of the NES classics. And a stalker that only moves when you look away. Don't let your flame go out.

items.title: Le Tapis Vert
items.description: Belote, Solitaire, Backgammon, Yatzy, Sudoku… 24 card and board games gathered on one green table. Play solo against the computer, pass-and-play with friends, or online with a friend. No ads, no microtransactions.

items.title: Sutja
items.description: A surreal poker roguelite. Stack power cards, attach stickers, reshape your deck, and push Chips × Mult to absurd heights. Face strange bosses, then follow the Journey into questions about choice, art, and what it means to play.

items.title: The WHEELJAM Collection
items.description: A collection of over 20 games making up submissions from the WHEELJAM game jams in 2025 and 2026.

items.title: Sinners Please
items.description: Only for sinners. ADMIT or SHOOT. You guard the gate of Hell. Check the papers, X-ray the bags and decide their fate. Some of them are sneaking in from heaven. We only want the sinners! Miss the rent, and Satan collects.

items.title: Bio Inc. Classic
items.description: Cowboy bank-robber in DEEP SPACE! You are Tom the famous space-bank robber. Going from station to station, taking all the new credits you can fit into your digital device, and buying whatever you see in front of you. The Space Cop animals are hot on your trial. Run, jump, and shoot your way to renegade freedom in this futuristic thriller! Killer graphics and game-play and a booming soundtrack make this a sure download for you today!

items.title: MORROWTAPE
items.description: A first-person psychological horror game set beneath a condemned 1989 telephone archive. Tune impossible calls, evade a creature that hunts every sound you make, and decide which evidence the city is allowed to remember.

items.title: Tetherlight
items.description: Tetherlight is a side-scrolling action adventure with a star-fox tether companion. Chain aerial movement and staff combat, confront twisted guardians, and plan your journey through a changing world to break its repeating nights.

items.title: Ball Bugz
items.description: Ball Bugs is an incremental defense game where you start with a single persistent ball and build up an arsenal of ball firing turrets, artillery and special ball types. Bounce, splat, upgrade and come back stronger until the bugs stop getting through.

items.title: Ferrite Runner
items.description: Ferrite Runner is a mouse-only cyberpunk extraction RPG with active-time combat. Fight waves and bosses, manage energy and thirst, and escape with your loot. Upgrade your gear and outposts between runs. Trade sealed crates or open them for equipment, then risk your loadout on another run.

items.title: A Deriva
items.description: A fisherman lives on your computer's taskbar. He fishes on his own while you work, from the Araguaia to the sea off Noronha. You glance over now and then, click when one bites, and buy a bigger boat. It also runs as a wallpaper.

items.title: ReGLOSS: CROSS
items.description: HI, fungame,play itGame features:-40 levels to play-9 different enemies-4 roles

items.title: Dealer's Tell: All Bets Are Final
items.description: A roguelite deduction game at a blackjack table. The devil deals - and cheats by a secret rule, a new one every floor. Watch the hands, cross out the suspects and name his scheme before suspicion closes in. Fifteen floors down, new house rules every run. A wrong guess costs your soul.

items.title: JosPlays - Gemhaven
items.description: Match glowing Heartstones to rebuild a forgotten valley. Swap gems, meet each level's goals before you run out of moves, and watch a whole city rise, from a humble hut to the shining Crown Castle, across a 15-level story campaign.

items.title: A Bad Dream: Trypophobia
items.description: Bad Ninja HD comes with typical jumping gameplay but wit lot more to face on the way!Bad Ninja HD is a skill game, in which the goal is to get the highest floor of the castle. Fight or avoid other ninjas on the way or choose Death. Collect items to help you climb as high as possible. And above all enjoy it.Just tap to change the wall, grab the power ups on the way, use them at you're advantage. Amazing graphics, various funny characters and great music will help you more to enjoy this game.

items.title: Rescue the Hostages: Twenty Deadly Questions
items.description: The mad bomber is back with a deadly game of twenty questions. Ask questions, uncover the words, disarm the bomb, and rescue the hostages in this gripping FMV horror experience where every decision could mean the difference between life or death.

items.title: Double Check
items.description: Fruit Flow is a Casual puzzle game. Colorful fruits, how many do you recognize? It can also help kids to classify the fruits, Which one with which one is the same Enjoy your leisure time by sliding your finger!Match them FREE!!!Fruit flow Features,**Multiple models for you to enjoy;**Endless model for you to challage, how far can you go?**Simply rule, link the same fruits together;**Easy and fun to play, but a challenge to fully master;**Time alert;**Share it with your friends.If you have idea about it, you can feedback to us, we are appreciated to it!!!Thanks all for support!!!
